Subject: MSA + Order Form — questions on auto-renew and convenience termination

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for walking us through the platform last week. Our legal/procurement teams reviewed the MSA and Order Form and sent a redline (attached) with two items we need clarity on before we proceed:

1) Auto-renew: The MSA currently auto-renews for successive 12-month terms unless either party provides 60 days' notice. We typically require a 90-day notice window for renewals at our enterprise tier. Can Redwood accommodate a 90-day opt-out for annual renewal (or confirm if 60 days is non-negotiable)?

2) Termination for convenience: The Order Form references Redwood's standard convenience termination right with a 30-day notice. For large accounts, we ask for either a 90-day winding down period or liquidated damages capped at one month of committed spend to cover migration. Is Redwood willing to accept a cap or extend the notice period?

We've attached our annotated MSA (ACME_MSA_Redline_v3.docx) for reference. Procurement would like to understand what concessions, if any, require exec approval vs. what your standard playbook supports. Our target is to sign by early June pending alignment.

Appreciate a quick confirmation and who on your side will handle the legal redline.

Best,

Karthik / team — reviewed the attached redline and summarized options below. I attached a short markup with suggested language (RB_Markup_MSATermination.docx).

Summary / recommendation (short):
- Auto-renew: we can accept a 90-day notice to opt out of renewal for the annual term for Enterprise accounts. This is a negotiated concession (no exec approval required if ARR < $250k; above that, we escalate to RevOps). Proposed clause: "Either party may elect not to renew by providing written notice at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Term."

- Termination for convenience: two pragmatic paths to offer the customer — choose one in the Order Form
  a) 90-day notice to terminate for convenience (customer bears usage charges during the 90-day winding period); OR
  b) 30-day notice with an Early Termination Fee (ETF) equal to the lesser of (i) one (1) month of the average monthly committed spend on the Order Form; or (ii) $50,000.

Rationale: Path (a) is operationally clean for both sides for migration planning; path (b) keeps our ability to recover ramp/commitment costs while giving the buyer a predictable cap. We commonly accept either approach depending on account size.

Redlines / next steps:
- I propose we offer Amco both options and let them pick. If they choose b) and the notional ETF exceeds $50k (example: very large deals), we will need RevOps sign-off. Aditya, please confirm threshold handling and whether Sales leadership signoff is required for ARRs above threshold.

- If acceptable, Sales can update the Order Form and I can approve the final MSA addendum. Otherwise, escalate to RevOps for exception.

Copying suggested language from the markup for insertion: 
"Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate the Order Form for convenience by providing written notice to the other party as set forth in the Order Form. Customer may select, at the time of execution of the Order Form, either (i) a ninety (90) day notice period for termination for convenience, during which Customer will remain responsible for charges for Services used and committed; or (ii) a thirty (30) day notice period together with an Early Termination Fee equal to the lesser of one (1) month of Customer's average monthly committed spend during the prior three (3) months under the Order Form or fifty thousand U.S. dollars (USD 50,000)."

I also flagged: audit trail, data export timing, and responsibilities for KV cache handover in the operational checklist — these are operational items that should be included in the Order Form addendum or a migration exhibit so the customer knows what to expect.

Attachment: RB_Markup_MSATermination.docx (contains inline redlines and the suggested fallback language).
